title: MEEK: Re-thinking Heterogeneous Parallel Error Detection Architecture for Real-World OoO Superscalar Processors
problem: Heterogeneous parallel error detection requires gathering data cross-chip from many core components to re-execute software, but integrating this into commodity out-of-order superscalar cores creates design complexity and risks heavy modifications to mature microarchitectures.
motivation: Fault tolerance is critical as chips integrate more transistors at smaller scales, but existing error-detection designs incur substantial overhead and require extensive re-engineering of production processors.
method: MEEK implements heterogeneous parallel error detection via co-designed hardware-software layers: a high-performance OoO core executes speculatively while power-efficient auxiliary cores re-execute the same code; coordinating software and light OS-level modifications orchestrate comparison and error reporting with microsecond-level latency. The design avoids invasive changes by partitioning responsibilities across ISA, microarchitecture, and operating system.
key_novelty: First full-RTL implementation of heterogeneous parallel error detection in an open-source SoC that achieves microsecond-scale fault detection with minimal architectural disruption via codesigned hardware-software partitioning.
contributions: Full-RTL design of MEEK integrated into an open-source SoC with microarchitecture, ISA, OS, and programming model support.
Identification and resolution of bottlenecks and bugs overlooked in prior theoretical work.
Demonstration of microsecond-level detection capacity with light changes to mature out-of-order cores.

metrics.other: microsecond-level detection latency, light design overhead

primary_theme: fault-tolerant processor design via parallel error detection
